title: Instrument choice and geographic clustering in the Galician literacy panel
abstract: We reconstruct a four-census panel used to estimate how historic emigration affected literacy in Galicia. In the versioned replication package, the archived coefficient and its printed diagnostics use different sets of instruments. Holding 1,284 observations and the controls fixed, we compare the two specifications. Restricted wild bootstrap tests grouped by 47 judicial districts give p=0.1246 for the instrument used to estimate the coefficient and p=0.0282 for the two instruments used in the diagnostics. The sign of the estimated coefficient survives each single-municipality deletion. These results concern inference in one historical literacy equation.
